message: <||completion||> Streaming code semantics directly from cheat.sh into your terminal core.

message: <||completion||> Image downloaded successfully into your current directory.

arguments.command: kw='<||string||>' && enc_kw=$(echo -n "$kw" | sed 's/ /+/g') && search_res=$(curl -s -A 'Mozilla/5.0' "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&list=search&srsearch=$enc_kw&format=json&origin=*") && title=$(echo "$search_res" | grep -o '"title":"[^"]*' | head -n 1 | cut -d'"' -f4) && if [ -z "$title" ]; then echo "⛔ No Wikipedia article found for $kw"; else enc_title=$(echo -n "$title" | sed 's/ /+/g') && img_res=$(curl -s -A 'Mozilla/5.0' "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&titles=$enc_title&prop=pageimages&piprop=original&format=json&origin=*") && img_url=$(echo "$img_res" | grep -o '"source":"[^"]*' | head -n 1 | cut -d'"' -f4) && if [ -z "$img_url" ]; then echo "⚠️ Article '$title' found, but has no original image."; else clean_name=$(echo "$title" | tr ' /' '__' | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9__-').jpg && out_path="./$clean_name" && echo "📥 Downloading image for '$title' into current folder..." && curl -s -A 'Mozilla/5.0' "$img_url" -o "$out_path" && echo "🎯 Saved to: $out_path" && termy_set_context active_file "$(cd "$(dirname "$out_path")" && pwd)/$(basename "$out_path")" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi; fi
arguments.explanation: Searches Wikipedia for the keyword, extracts the top article title, fetches its original image URL, downloads it directly into the current working directory, and updates termy's active_file context with the absolute path.
arguments.goal: Download specific Wikipedia image into the current directory and register it in context

thinking: The primate wants the file visible right under their nose, not hidden in the system's ephemeral memory. Storing it in the current working directory using a cleaned up file name.

Using pwd to dynamically register the absolute path into active_file context, so if the user shifts directories later, the file reference won't break when passed to other tools like wallpaper setters.

 sed 's/ /+/g'

 head -n 5
) && if [ -z "$res" ]; then 
 printf '⛔ No Wikipedia article found for: %s\n' '<||string||>';
